Guides

DTF Printing Guides & Resources

Everything we tell customers over the counter — now written down so you can prep your files right the first time.

How to Prep Your Artwork for DTF Printing

Getting your file right the first time saves a round of back-and-forth before your gang sheet goes to print. Here's what we look for:

  • File type: Transparent PNG, TIFF, or vector PDF work best. If you only have a JPEG or need cleanup, send what you have — we can help prep it.
  • Resolution: 300 DPI at the size you want it printed. Scaling up a low-res image will show on press.
  • Background: Keep it transparent unless the design is meant to have a solid background — DTF only prints what's in the file.
  • Color matching: Share Pantone references or product photos if brand color accuracy matters, and we'll dial in the color profile before printing.
  • Layout: No minimums on gang sheets — use the Gang Sheet Builder

Recommended Heat Press Settings for DTF Transfers

Every transfer we send out includes a cheat sheet, but here's the baseline setting that works for most fabrics:

  • Temperature: 285°F
  • Time: 12 seconds
  • Pressure: Medium

Peel cold once the transfer has cooled for the cleanest release. If you're pressing a heat-sensitive fabric (like some polyester blends), test on a scrap piece first or contact us — we're happy to walk through settings for your specific garment.
